implementation: e2e/environment.py adds explicit reset and a persistent incomplete-reset barrier. Removal checks exact ownership/shared resources before stopping all runtime/setup producers, verifies stopped PIDs and removed container IDs/network namespaces, then verifies volume users absent before exact owned-volume removal. Fresh setup uses the normal image/migration. Empty current V1 schema/writer and adapter v1/default/zero-delivery checks precede handoff; rebuilding failures remove handoff/relay, retain diagnostics and require explicit reset rather than wait/restart. Cleanup reuses the same verified quiescence/removal path.

scripts/check-e2e-reset.py drives the public CLI for repeated dirty, active-connection and failed-environment resets, real migration/startup refusal/recovery, foreign shared-mount refusal, new baseline/pinned-byte checks and retained post-reset restart. It reuses prior lifecycle provider-byte/private-admin/egress regressions. Test-owned probe SQL/configuration faults are lower-layer infrastructure checks, not app initialization or game/action injection.

ComposeIsolationTest keeps a separate normal real Testcontainers PostgreSQL migration, sentinel, open transaction and JDBC connectivity check alive throughout the reset suite. It checks unrelated inventories and cleanup isolation in both directions with exact owned resources. server/build.gradle.kts gives it an explicit composeIsolationTest task while retaining all ordinary server tests in test; no added dependency, runtime type/API or clean-image build cycle.

18 controller/topology/relay unit tests include no-delete-before-quiescence, foreign-target refusal, incomplete-reset wait/restart barriers and safe capture/reset failure behavior. All 34 ordinary service/database and six shared JVM tests pass after the build-task change; actual XML has no skips/errors/failures.

e2e/README.md documents exact commands, reset versus retained restart, baseline and pending/completed records, failure/ownership limits, future-worker/store obligations and unchanged two-loopback-endpoint Android handoff. No UI-document publication is applicable.
evidenceNotes: The initial successful isolation run used an explicitly filtered server:test before the dedicated task existed. The final successful run uses the separate composeIsolationTest task with no build cache and normal strict locks. They are two distinct complete real-image qualifications, not retries masking a red check.

The final qualification initially copied actual JUnit XML to an untracked XML file. It contained original trailing whitespace. Before staging, the retention helper was extended to encode all final isolation/server/shared XML losslessly in junit-results.json, preserving each original byte hash and text rather than altering command output or weakening whitespace checks. The obsolete untracked XML copy was removed; decoding its record reproduces the exact hash printed by isolation-final. The executed --retain-only command separately validates this packaging; it does not claim another test run. No product/build source changed after final successful qualification/regressions.

Required checks pass; expected CLI failure cases inside the successful qualification assert their nonzero exits, absent ready handoffs/barriers and real diagnostics. No skipped/red required validation is labeled passing. Successful initial development outputs remain diagnostic history rather than substituting for final checks.

No paid/external provider, deployment, subagent, another loop or permission/model/authorization change occurred.
